working_title: Is the Agent Fragile, or the Benchmark Stateful? Auditing Task-Order Effects in Self-Improving Web Agents
problem_statement: Task-order stress tests for self-improving agents jointly perturb the agent's learning history and the persistent environment history of a stateful benchmark. In WebArena, earlier benchmark tasks can mutate the service state that defines later task truth, so a shuffled run can be scored against reference text tied to an earlier backend state.

closest_work.difference: Reports AWM/ReasoningBank task-order fragility and attributes part of it to memory underspecification; does not separate memory-order effects from persistent WebArena environment carryover.

DynamicMCPBench argues that fixed ground truth is fragile on live stateful servers and uses effect-based scoring; it does not audit published self-improvement order experiments or quantify environment-order confounding in WebArena.
ClawMark deliberately models evolving service state with deterministic post-state checkers; our work diagnoses unintended cross-task state carryover in an existing self-improvement stress test.
WebArena provides executable stateful websites and task evaluators; our contribution is a longitudinal cross-task contamination audit under shuffled evaluation streams.

novelty_claim: We introduce the first source-grounded causal and retrospective audit, under the current literature search, showing how a published self-improving-agent task-order stress test couples memory evolution to benchmark environment evolution and quantifying the resulting change in the reported order gap.
contributions: A causal decomposition of task-order stress testing into agent-memory history and persistent-environment history, with a machine-readable task interference audit.
A direct released-trajectory certificate: a scorer-failed task can still mutate the backend, after which a later task correctly reads current state but fails against stale fixed ground truth.
A replicated high-precision sentinel panel across AWM and ReasoningBank: three dynamic-reference tasks pass 18/18 ordinal evaluations and 0/36 shuffled evaluations.

A conservative full WebArena retrospective over 84 run-domain cells: 887 lower-bound exposed sensitive-reader units in memory shuffles, including 424 failures; state-sensitive-task exclusion reduces AWM's observed shuffle gap by 34.6-44.5% and ReasoningBank's by 14.9-17.5%, while a substantial residual remains.

A state-isolated order-stress protocol recommendation: separate agent-history randomization from environment-history randomization using per-task environment restoration or state-conditioned/effect-based evaluators, and include a shuffled no-memory control.

strongest_alternative_explanations.name: memory_only_fragility
strongest_alternative_explanations.test: Remove state-sensitive readers and measure residual shuffle gap.
strongest_alternative_explanations.result: Residual remains: AWM 2.46/3.36 pp; RBank 6.48/6.11 pp.

strongest_alternative_explanations.name: generic_run_variance
strongest_alternative_explanations.test: Three runs x two methods x two shuffle seeds on predefined dynamic-reference tasks.
strongest_alternative_explanations.result: All ordinal method-run units pass while all shuffled counterparts fail for each of three sentinels.

strongest_alternative_explanations.name: agent_misread_current_state
strongest_alternative_explanations.test: Match writer and reader released logs by item identity/order total/current status.
strongest_alternative_explanations.result: Task 509 produces the Cole Haan order; task 96 later reads the matching order as Pending but is scored against the old canceled-order gold.

strongest_alternative_explanations.name: environment_contamination_explains_everything
strongest_alternative_explanations.test: State-sensitive exclusion and future shuffled no-memory/per-task-reset control.
strongest_alternative_explanations.result: Large residual remains; shuffled no-memory/per-task-reset control is not yet executed.

claim_experiment_matrix.claim: Order permutation changes persistent benchmark environment history in addition to memory history.
Released shuffled trajectories contain direct ground-truth invalidation caused by earlier state-changing tasks.
Dynamic-reference failures replicate across memory methods, runs, and shuffle seeds.
State-sensitive tasks account for a material fraction of the measured order gap, with the largest reduction observed for AWM. Residual order sensitivity remains after the exclusion.
Environment carryover fully explains the original paper's task-order fragility.
A state-isolated order-stress protocol with a matched shuffled no-memory control separates memory-history sensitivity from environment-history sensitivity under the same execution stack.

baselines.description: Released AWM/ReasoningBank shuffle1 and shuffle2 runs.
Recompute order gap after excluding preregistered state-sensitive dynamic-reference readers.
No-memory agent under the same shuffle seeds and stateful execution protocol; not present in released experiments and not executable on current infrastructure without a local WebArena image.
Per-task restored environment with identical order permutations; future validation, not needed for the narrow retrospective claim.
